messages:
sam: Heads up — canary in us-west-2 showing a p95 spike from 110ms -> 620ms and errors ~5% for text-generation route since ~10:02 UTC. Seeing increased queue length on runtime.
deploy-bot: [AUTOMATION] Deployment v2.4.0 rolled to canary (40% traffic) at 2026-03-20T10:00:12Z. Observability rule triggered: latency_regression. Details: https://dash/reports/abc123
caroline: ugh. is this noisy or a real regression? any correlation with the quantized backend change in this build?
raj: I pulled logs — a lot of kv-cache misses and OOM retries on a subset of pods (nodepool-qa-3). Looks like a memory growth pattern with longer seqs.
adele: if it's OOM-related we should not auto-rollback across all regions. Prefer targeted revert on canary hosts so we don't affect prod.
ops-sre: agree with adele. We can pin traffic back off the canary pool + repro pod logs. Two-step: (1) drain canary pods from LB, (2) scale canary deployment to 0 for the new image, (3) restart with previous image v2.3.9. I can run the commands but need someone to approve swift comms.
maria: I'll draft a short status update for #incidents and statuspage if we revert. Keep it concise: "Investigating performance regression in canary; rolling back canary rollout to reduce customer impact." 
sam: ok ops-sre, go ahead with targeted revert. i'll monitor metrics and take ownership of the postmortem. @caroline @maria please prep comms.
deploy-bot: CURRENT_ROLLOUT -> {"version":"v2.4.0","canary_percent":"40","regions":["us-west-2","eu-central-1"]}
ops-sre: executing. command sequence:
```bash
# drain canary from LB
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/inference-api inference-api=redwood/inference:v2.3.9 --selector=rollout=canary
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-api --selector=rollout=canary
# scale down new replica set if needed
kubectl -n inference scale rs inference-api-v2-4-0 --replicas=0 || true
```
ops-sre: started step 1 (image set + restart) at 10:06 UTC. watching pod statuses.
sam: copying logs to the thread: worked on a failed pod -> `OOMKilled` with stack pointing at attention_cache.cc:142.
caroline: thanks — that matches the kv-cache miss theory. Good call on targeted revert instead of full auto-rollback.
ops-sre: rollback applied to canary subset; new pods coming up with v2.3.9. LB healthchecks passing. Confirming metrics ingestion.
deploy-bot: [ACTION] Canary revert complete. New canary image: v2.3.9. Canary traffic now at 0% for v2.4.0 (remaining 60% still on v2.3.9). Summary: rollback_success=true; timestamp=2026-03-20T10:09:15Z
sam: p95 dropped back to ~120ms within two minutes. errors down to 0.7%.
maria: posting to #incidents and statuspage now. message: "We reverted the canary rollout for v2.4.0 after a performance regression was detected. No broader customer impact observed. Engineers are investigating root cause; we'll follow up with a postmortem and timeline." :mega:
adele: follow-ups: (1) add preflight synthetic with longer seqs to canary check, (2) add memory cap alert per nodepool, (3) hold v2.4.0 from automated promotion until root cause fixed. I'll file the tickets.
caroline: also add a gating rule to block quantization changes without a kseq long-run test.
sam: noted. I'll own the postmortem. assign to ops + eng-ml. timeline: immediate triage today, RCA draft by EOD tomorrow.
maria: adding comms: internal note to sales/solutions and support with pointer to statuspage.
ops-sre: leaving the canary pool on v2.3.9 and marking the v2.4.0 rollout as paused. tagging resources in the deploy board.
caroline: thank you everyone. quick retro in #eng-releases tomorrow 10:30 to lock down rollout gating changes. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [DEPLOY BOARD] rollout v2.4.0 -> status: PAUSED (reason: canary_regression). Ticket: DPL-4821
sam: closing thread once postmortem link is in. good job on the quick targeted revert, saved customers from a full rollback.
